vakbeschrijving.nl:
The goal of the course is twofold. First, students will learn to work with new sensing techniques from earth observation and geophysics that extend their knowledge from Year 1. These techniques include multispectral and seismic imaging techniques. Second, after this course, students will have obtained the knowledge and skills to critically derive information from uncertain 2D Earth System data.  

Students will get acquainted with the concept of spatial analysis and students will be trained in acquisition, processing, and analysis of 2D Earth System data.  Building on the fundamentals acquired in previous courses of the Earth System Data learning line (Grand Challenges, Geodata Fundamentals, Signals and Time Series), students will advance their skills towards notably imaging systems and two-dimensional datasets.  

 Image acquisition systems provide spatial data that varies in terms of coverage and volume, quality, and complexity.  In the Sensing and Spatial Analysis course, students will learn to work with processing techniques to estimate variable properties and the uncertainties in these estimates at a given spatial location. These processing techniques incorporate spatial variability, data uncertainty and scales in different ways and include deterministic and stochastic interpolation, 2D Fourier analysis, supervised and unsupervised classification, and spatial filtering and smoothing.  

Students will use the different spatial processing methods on data from known and newly introduced sensing techniques. Students will notably learn about principles and properties of multispectral remote sensing and geophysical data, while students will apply spatial analysis techniques on known sensor data such as   meteorological data, GNSS, photogrammetry and laser scanning. Students will learn to use QGIS and Python as tools to work with realistic scenarios of spatial analysis using data sets consisting of thousands to millions of observations.  

This course is directly related to the 2nd years Fieldwork Project, that runs in the same semester. Students will process multispectral remote sensing data in the Fieldwork Project using methods introduced in this course.

leerdoelen.nl:
[LO1] Explain the physical and technical principles behind spatial sensing techniques including multispectral remote sensing and geophysical techniques.

[LO2] Apply spatial analysis techniques in an efficient workflow on real spatial data of various data types using a GIS system and Python.

[LO3] Evaluate spatial sensor techniques against each other in terms of coverage and sampling schemes, effort required, and quality.

[LO4] Apply different mathematical and statistical techniques to assess spatial continuity, variability and scales.

[LO5] Estimate uncertainty of spatial measurements and derived parameters.

[LO6] Differentiate between different spatial analysis methods of interpolation, classification, smoothing and filtering in terms of computational efficiency, robustness, ease of use and quality of results.

toetsing.nl:
• 60% Assignments

  • 40% Exam (1.5h), closed-book (week 4.3, resit week 4.10)

In case the Assignments grade is below 5.8, it is possible to opt for individual replacement assignment. The maximum grade for the Assignments component that can be obtained is then a grade 6.0.

In order to pass the course, the final grade must be a 5.8, and at least a 5.0 must be obtained per component.

toelichting_onderwijsmethode.nl:
course activities consist of lectures, exercise classes, assignments, and one afternoon of data gathering. 

  • During the lectures, concepts are explained, in discussion with the students. Lectures will include formative exercises 

  • During the exercise classes, students will work on exercises and assignments applying course concepts. Students will be assisted in installing the QGIS software on their own laptop and use it together with Python for spatial data analysis. Some of these data + techniques will be part of the Y2 fieldwork assignment. 

  • Students will gather in situ training data, geophysical and multi-spectral data around Delft from data repositories and using their Smartphone as sensor
